anchors.finding: Standard errors take sqrt diagonal; debiased p-values use t(df_resid), otherwise normal
Confidence intervals use residual df rather than cluster-count df when debiased
Dense least squares uses scipy gelsy with max(shape)*machine epsilon cutoff
Sparse effect projection extracts lsmr coefficient only; local code does not retain solver termination diagnostics
Covariance scale subtracts extra_df and optionally regressors; residual and covariance degrees of freedom can differ

findings: Clustered covariance does not by itself select cluster-count reference degrees of freedom.
Sparse projection diagnostics require a wrapper contract; no claim that scipy lacks internal statuses.
Negative covariance diagonals require explicit handling before ordinary uncertainty reporting.
